items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1957-08-04
items.q: my brother was playing corner right there with him, with Johnny Lindsay, Herbert Lindsay, and his daddy was playing guitar.

ctx.x: That one place you mentioned where your brother played was at Hammonds? Hammonds. Hammonds. Hannah. Yes, sir.

Hammonds, that was on Murray, and Custom House. And when I started playing with Drew Oliver, we played in that Willie. I mean, they called Eddie Dorsey. He was our collector. He worked in the band somewhere in town, but he used to play bass, and he used to play guitar. But we taken him in to be our collector. That is at Hunters, right across from the Hammonds. We was playing right across from the Murray's brother over there after that. See, well, my brother was playing corner right there with him, with Johnny…
Yes, he played trowel. He played bass, so he's dead now, too.

items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: I don't know if he's in Chicago or where. Well I left, I left them in Chicago and I came back home.

ctx.x: That's what I heard. Yeah. Some people knew him, did you ever know a Mary Mack? You remember a vaudeville team, Mack and Mack? Yeah. Mary Mack. Yeah. She came from across the river. Fess knew her. Yeah. Minetta. And they're up in Chicago and they said they saw a Herbert Lindsay within the last, it'll be two years now. He could be dead by this time. Yeah. But I couldn't, they couldn't find him when I was there and I didn't, never did see him.
And I don't know if he's in Chicago or where. Well I left, I left them in Chicago and I came back home. I left them all over. The whole bank stayed up there.
The whole bank stayed up there.
